transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-09-15 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~68 minutes
Attendees: Olivia (Redwood AE), Marcus (CSM), Diego (SE) — Laura, Ethan, Priya, Anita, Samir (NorthPoint)

Summary (auto): Focus on onboarding requirements for a private / VPC-based deployment. High security bar, want pilot in staging then production. Action items captured.

[00:00] Olivia: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Olivia Park from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Marcus and Diego are joining from CS and engineering. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Laura: Hi Olivia, thanks. Laura Chen here, Head of ML at NorthPoint. We're excited to get this rolling.
[00:12] Priya: Priya Singh, CTO. We're short on time today, want to confirm the security and network plan first.
[00:18] Ethan: Ethan Murphy, infra. I'll be leading the VPC peering and firewall work.
[00:22] Anita: Anita Rao, legal — I'll flag contract items.
[00:25] Marcus: Quick agenda — intros, success criteria, security/compliance Qs, staging pilot scope, next steps. Sound good?
[00:29] Samir: Yep, makes sense.
[00:33] Olivia: Great. Laura, can you kick off with your top success metrics and timeline?
[00:37] Laura: Sure. Top line: latency under 120ms p95 for standard prompts, cost per 1k tokens needs to be competitive to our internal infra, and data never leaves our VPC for PII calls. Timeline — pilot in staging in two weeks, production go-live in mid-November if pilot goes well.
[00:52] Diego: Okay, when you say "data never leaves VPC" do you mean full private deployment with customer-managed control plane or would you accept a private peered deployment where control plane is hosted?
[01:02] Priya: We prefer control plane in our VPC. For compliance we need KMS integration + audit logs that are customer-visible.
[01:09] Marcus: Noted. Redwood offers private deployment options — we've seen two common patterns: private control plane in customer's VPC, or dedicated with VPC peering and strict egress rules. We'll walk through both.
[01:19] Olivia: Diego, quick overview of the deployment choices and what we recommend for NorthPoint?
[01:24] Diego: Sure. Option A is Redwood Private — we can run a control plane component in your VPC and optionally an on-prem connector if needed. Option B is Redwood Dedicated with private peering — the control plane stays in Redwood but the inference nodes are isolated to a dedicated tenant in the region. For strict data residency + KMS, Option A is cleaner. It supports customer-managed KMS, we do have HSM integrations but there's usually a short security review.
[01:47] Ethan: If we go Option A, what's the uplift on engineering effort from our side? We have a fairly locked-down network.
[01:54] Diego: On your side you'll need to provide a network diagram, open ports for management (we list specifics in the runbook), and provision an IAM role for the control plane to access your KMS. We'll provide IaC templates to make it repeatable.
[02:06] Laura: We will need to review the IaC before running. Also our legal team will need explicit BAA and data processing addenda references.
[02:14] Anita: Right, and we need to confirm retention windows for logs and any opt-out for storing prompts for training.
[02:22] Marcus: For retention — standard is configurable; for customers on Private we can set retention to your required windows and mark data as non-training. We'll capture those settings in the privacy addendum.
[02:34] Olivia: On SSO — do you use SAML or OIDC?
[02:37] Priya: We use Okta and SAML mostly, with a few OIDC apps.
[02:42] Diego: Okta + SAML is fully supported, we also support SCIM for user provisioning. We'll need your IdP metadata and a test user to validate.
[02:51] Samir: About monitoring and observability — how granular are the token-level cost breakdowns? We want per-route cost visibility.
[02:58] Marcus: The Redwood Console shows per-route and per-token breakdowns, you can tag tokens by product line. We'll also integrate tracing hooks if you want X-Ray/Datadog export.
[03:08] Ethan: Any concerns about throughput? During peak our traffic is bursty — 200 concurrent sessions with short prompts.
[03:15] Diego: Redwood's serving runtime does continuous batching; for short prompts bursts are fine but we'll size Dedicated pools for peak concurrency. As part of the staging benchmark we'll simulate that pattern.
[03:25] Laura: For the pilot we plan to run two datasets: 1) non-PII customer support corpus, and 2) a masked PII dataset to validate redaction. Will Redwood support on-the-fly redaction?
[03:36] Diego: We have a few redaction options. We recommend pre-processing to purge PII, but we can also plug in streaming redaction and private regex rules inside the VPC. Will need sample prompts to tune.
[03:47] Priya: Tokenization and cost — we need an estimate per 1k tokens for the model we'd likely pick. Can you ballpark now?
[03:54] Olivia: Ballpark depends on model and quantization. For a dedicated quantized LLM you'd see lower per-token costs vs hosted. We'll send a pricing matrix in the follow-up.
[04:04] Anita: Legal question — what audit logs do you keep? Are prompt texts stored in logs?
[04:10] Marcus: Audit logs capture request metadata and can optionally capture full prompt text. For Private we can configure prompt masking in logs and set full-text retention to 0 days if required.
[04:23] Laura: Ok good. Can you support customer-managed KMS where encryption keys never leave our control?
[04:28] Diego: Yes — customer-managed KMS is supported. For on-prem HSMs there's an extra integration step, but we've done it with a handful of finance customers.
[04:36] Samir: What's your SLA for Dedicated vs Private?
[04:39] Olivia: Dedicated has an SLA with predictable throughput and latency targets; Private SLAs are negotiated depending on hosting model but we typically support enterprise SLAs for Reserved commitments. I'll include the SLA language in the packet.
[04:53] [05:00] (short silence, crosstalk)
[05:12] Ethan: Let's talk timeline. Laura mentioned two-week staging pilot — is that realistic? We need at least two weeks to provision and validate network.
[05:21] Marcus: Two weeks for a basic staging is tight but possible if we have network details and samples today. Otherwise three weeks is more realistic.
[05:29] Priya: We can target three weeks.
[05:32] Diego: For the staging benchmark we'll need: sample prompt set (50-100 prompts), expected QPS pattern, and a list of success metrics (latency p95, error rate, cost targets).
[05:45] Laura: We'll share the prompt set and our quality rubric — we score responses on accuracy and hallucination rate.
[05:52] Olivia: Great. Marcus, outline the onboarding cadence you propose.
[05:56] Marcus: Week 0: kickoff (today). Week 1-2: infra & network setup, basic staging. Week 3: run benchmark and quality evals. Week 4: pilot with real workloads, iterate. After pilot we'll do a go/no-go review. I'll publish a sprint template to your team.
[06:19] Priya: What about rollback and fallback — if the model has a regression in LLM quality how does Redwood handle that in production?
[06:26] Diego: We support rollouts with canary + automatic fallback to a previous model or smaller cheaper variant. The console can detect regressions based on eval prompt sets and auto-fallback.
[06:38] Samir: That auto-fallback is important for us. Also interested in cost controls — can we set per-route budgets?
[06:45] Marcus: Yes, the platform supports per-route quotas and alerts when consumption reaches thresholds.
[06:52] Anita: Contract-wise, we need to confirm liability language for data leakage. I'll send Redlined clauses after the packet.
[06:59] Olivia: We'll coordinate legal and get answers — we have standard DPA/BAA language and can surface any custom requests.
[07:07] Laura: Any open-source model support? We have some internal experimentation with open-llama variants.
[07:12] Diego: We onboard open models frequently; kernel selection and quantization recommendations will be part of the Optimize toolkit. For production we usually recommend vetted variants Redwood-verified for stability.
[07:24] Ethan: Are there any blockers you foresee from Redwood's side?
[07:27] Diego: The main potential blocker is long security review for on-prem HSM integration — that typically takes a couple weeks. Otherwise the onboarding is straightforward if we get network artifacts.
[07:38] Marcus: Also provisioning Dedicated GPU pools can take a few days depending on region. We'll surface lead times in the runbook.
[07:45] Olivia: Let's confirm immediate deliverables: Marcus will share the runbook, Diego will schedule the staging benchmark, Olivia will send pricing and legal kickoff. Customer will share network diagram, IdP metadata, sample prompts, and redaction requirements.
[07:59] Priya: Quick nit — our compliance officer will want copies of SOC2 Type II and any penetration test reports you can share.
[08:06] Marcus: We'll attach SOC2 documentation and high-level pen test summary in the security packet. For deeper audits we can coordinate an SOC bridge call.
[08:16] Anita: We'll also request encryption-at-rest certificates and KMS flow diagrams.
[08:21] Diego: We'll include those in the technical pack.
[08:24] Samir: Curious — for observability, is there a way to export request traces to our existing APM?
[08:29] Marcus: Yes, you can forward traces to Datadog or X-Ray; we have an exporter.
[08:34] Laura: One last question on data residency — some EU customers require logs remain in-region. Can Private be region-locked?
[08:40] Diego: Yes, Private can be provisioned in-region and we can enforce log storage region. We'll need to know exact region requirements.
[08:50] Olivia: Okay, we're getting close on time. Any other burning questions?
[08:54] Priya: No more from me.
[08:56] Ethan: One small ask: can you provide a checklist for firewall rules so infra can pre-provision?
[08:59] Diego: Absolutely, that's in the runbook we'll share.
[09:03] Marcus: I'll put a quick checklist in the first email so you can start that work while the legal packet is reviewed.
[09:10] Olivia: Closing recap — runbook and sprint template from Marcus, staging benchmark/bench timeslot from Diego, pricing and SLA packet from me. Customer to send network diagram, IdP metadata, sample prompts, and legal redlines. We'll aim to have the staging environment ready in three weeks.
[09:27] Laura: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:31] Priya: Thanks.
[09:33] Olivia: Thank you all, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the technical deep dive.
[09:38] (call ends)
